newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Trade suspended in Cyprus Airways.
newsitem.headline: Trade suspended in Cyprus Airways.

text.p: Trading in shares of national carrier Cyprus Airways was suspended by the Cyprus Stock Exchange on Tuesday after demand broke through a 15 percent volatility limit, traders said.

The last transaction in Cyprus Airways was made at 40.4 cents on Tuesday amid heavy volume of 50,600 shares changing hands before trading in the company was automatically suspended. The previous transaction in Cyprus Airways shares had been at 34.7 cents on Monday.
"From the first deal the 15 percent volatility limit of the exchange was exceeded," one floor trader told Reuters.

Officials of the stock exchange were not immediately available for comment on how long the suspension would last, though other market players said the move was just a formality and trading would resume at the next session on Wednesday.

The unusual rally on shares in the debt-ridden airline, whose chairman warned only last month could face bankruptcy before the turn of the century, was the culmination of a gradual rise in the price of shares over the past 10 days.
Market sources said the buyer was an existing shareholder interested in expanding his hold in the company.
Airline officials declined to comment on the steep rise in the price of the share.
"Well, its impressive. We had noticed the price was going up," said a company source.

Tuesday's closing price is the highest the airline has reached in months, ever since a profit warning was issued last year, and later disclosures of a consolidated preliminary pre-tax loss of 2.15 million pounds in 1996.
The company, which is 80 percent owned by the government, with the remainder traded on the Cyprus stock exchange, had posted pre-tax profits of 5.03 million pounds in 1995.

Just last month, airline chairman Takis Kyriakides publicly admitted Cyprus Airways is looking at a 7.0 million pound loss in 1997, and possible bankruptcy by 1999 if drastic measures are not taken to reverse its dire finances.
